title: Open extension by zero and restriction for sheaf dg modules
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal S$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal C$ a sheaf dg $\mathcal S$-algebra. Use the left modules, signed shifts, cone triangles and localizations $K_X(\mathcal C)$ and $D_X(\mathcal C)$ of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any open inclusion. Degreewise extension by zero of the underlying module sheaves has a canonical dg $\mathcal C$-action extending the given action on $U$, with zero stalk outside $U$. Together with degreewise restriction $j^*$ it preserves dg homotopies and underlying quasi-isomorphisms and induces additive functors
$$j_!:D_U(\mathcal C|_U)\rightleftarrows D_X(\mathcal C):j^*.$$
Both functors preserve the specified signed shifts and distinguished cone triangles (including their isomorphic localized images). There is a natural adjunction
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D_X(\mathcal C)}(j_!P,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D_U(\mathcal C|_U)}(P,j^*Q),$$
whose unit $P\to j^*j_!P$ is the canonical isomorphism and whose counit $j_!j^*Q\to Q$ restricts to the identity on $U$ under that isomorphism.
For every open inclusion $k:V\hookrightarrow X$, put $T=U\cap V$, $j':T\hookrightarrow V$ and $k':T\hookrightarrow U$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$k^*j_!\simeq j'_!k'^*.$$
For nested opens $W\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism $(ji)_!\simeq j_!i_!$. These identifications are induced by degreewise extension by zero and restriction, commute with the adjunction units and counits, and are coherent under further open restrictions and compositions: all iterated identifications with the same degreewise sheaf map agree. No boundedness, flatness, quasi-coherence or perfectness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0FRA (lemma-extension-by-zero-graded), 0FRV (section-localize-dg) and 0FRW (lemma-extension-by-zero-dg), specialized to opens of a topological space and transported from right to signed left modules; exactness uses modules.tex Tag 01AK (lemma-j-shriek-exact). The localized adjunction and restriction/coherence assertions are independent consequences to be proved, not assertions that the cited Hom formula alone already supplies them.

proof.text: Write $J=j_!$ and $R=j^*$. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-adjunction] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal O=\mathcal S$: its degreewise sheafified presheaf construction gives the left dg action, differential, functor $J$ and ordinary dg adjunction $J\dashv R$. Its underlying degreewise module sheaves are the ordinary extensions by zero, since the defining presheaf in each degree is the extension-by-zero presheaf. Thus [lem-sc-module-extension-by-zero-stalk-maps](1) gives $(JP)^n_x=P^n_x$ for $x\in U$ and zero otherwise. The adjunction map sends $f:JP\to Q$ to $R(f)\eta_P$, with $\eta$ induced by the identity of $P$ on opens contained in $U$. Consequently $\eta_P:P\to RJP$ is degreewise the identity under the canonical restriction identification. The counit $\varepsilon_Q:JRQ\to Q$ restricts to the identity on $U$, because its transpose is $1_{RQ}$. These are dg maps by the cited dg adjunction.

Both degreewise module functors are additive and exact by [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact]; here $(X,\mathcal S)$ is a ringed space, with no local-ring hypothesis. They preserve underlying quasi-isomorphisms: exactness identifies the image of each kernel and image of a differential with the kernel and image of the transported differential, hence identifies $F(H^nM)$ with $H^n(FM)$ for $F=J,R$. Applying $F$ to the cohomology isomorphisms of a quasi-isomorphism therefore again gives cohomology isomorphisms, for every integer $n$. This argument uses no boundedness or flatness.

A signed degree $r$ graded map $h$ on $U$ extends degreewise by zero: before sheafification it is $h$ on opens contained in $U$ and zero on the other opens. Thus $J(h)(am)=(-1)^{r|a|}aJ(h)(m)$; this is an identity of presheaf maps and hence of their induced sheaf maps. Restriction has the same property. Applying either additive degreewise functor $F=J,R$ to $f-g=d h+h d$ gives $Ff-Fg=d(Fh)+(Fh)d$, so it preserves dg homotopies and induces an additive functor on $K$. For the adjunction of step 1, a homotopy $h:JP\to Q$ transposes to $Rh\circ\eta_P$, still signed degree $-1$, and a homotopy $t:P\to RQ$ transposes to $\varepsilon_Q\circ Jt$. Their boundaries transpose in the same way since $\eta,\varepsilon$ are chain maps. The two inverse ordinary dg Hom bijections therefore induce inverse Hom bijections on homotopy classes, giving $J\dashv R$ on $K$ with the same unit and counit.

source.place: Tag 0FRW (lemma-extension-by-zero-dg), compatibility with differentials; signed homotopies as defined in the item

proof.text: For either $F=J,R$, the degreewise identity $F(M[k])\cong(FM)[k]$ respects differentials $(-1)^kd$ and actions $(-1)^{k|a|}a m$. Additivity gives $F(N\oplus M[1])\cong FN\oplus(FM)[1]$. In these coordinates the cone differential on both sides is $(n,m)\mapsto(dn+F(f)m,-dm)$, and the left action on the second summand has the same factor $(-1)^{|a|}$. This identifies $F(C(f))$ with $C(Ff)$ as dg modules. It also sends inclusion $i$ to $i$ and the specified final map $-p$ to $-p$. Hence the cone triangles and shifts specified in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization] are preserved, as are triangles isomorphic to them.

source.place: Tag 0FS5 (definition-cone), with the left signed shifts fixed in def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization

proof.text: To apply the right-module homotopy-system theorem to the chosen left convention, form the graded opposite dg algebra $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $a*b=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$ and the same differential. Give a left module $M$ the right action $m*a=(-1)^{|m||a|}am$. Associativity follows since the total sign in either $(m*a)*b$ or $m*(a*b)$ is $|m|(|a|+|b|)+|a||b|$ before the term $ba m$. The Leibniz rule gives $d(m*a)=dm*a+(-1)^{|m|}m*da$. A signed degree $r$ left map satisfies $h(m*a)=(-1)^{|m||a|+r|a|}a h(m)=h(m)*a$, so it is an ordinary right graded map. The inverse construction is $am=(-1)^{|m||a|}m*a$. On $M[k]$, the two signs $(-1)^{(|m|-k)|a|}$ and $(-1)^{k|a|}$ cancel to give the unchanged right action; cone actions consequently match as well. Thus this identity on underlying complexes identifies exactly the homotopies, shifts, cones and quasi-isomorphisms of the two conventions.

The open site of $X$ (and of each open subspace) is small in the universes fixed in the item. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-homotopy-system] to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ on that site and use the explicit identification of step 5. Thus each chosen left-module $K$ is triangulated with exactly the signed cone triangles, and its underlying quasi-isomorphisms form a compatible multiplicative system. Apply [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] to this system: the word localization $D$ of the item has the triangulated structure with additive exact localization functor $Q$, and its distinguished triangles are exactly the isomorphic images of the specified cone triangles. This uses the compatible-system assertion of the homotopy-system node, rather than claiming triangulatedness from the definition alone.

By steps 2 and 3, $Q_XJ$ and $Q_UR$ invert quasi-isomorphisms. The factorization assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] induces functors $\bar J:D_U\to D_X$ and $\bar R:D_X\to D_U$ with their canonical factorizations. For the word presentation these functors send a word to the word of images, including $w^{-1}\mapsto F(w)^{-1}$. Each is additive by [lem-pur-additive-localization-descent], applied with source $K$, localization $Q$, additive functor $QF$ and target the other $D$: all categories are additive by step 6, $Q$ is additive, and every object of the word localization is already a $Q$-image. The shift isomorphisms of step 4 descend by the natural-transformation assertion of the localization universal property. Step 4 also shows directly that localized cone triangles go to localized cone triangles; the functors preserve their isomorphic images because functors preserve isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization); natural-transformation universal property as stated by the cited node

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to the adjunction on $K$ from step 3 and the two functor factorizations from step 7. It supplies $\bar J\dashv\bar R$ on the entire unbounded localized categories, with unit and counit the images of the original unit and counit under these factorizations. The unit is an isomorphism since step 1 made it an actual dg isomorphism; the restricted counit is still the identity by step 1 and functoriality of localization. This proves the requested derived Hom bijection, without assuming that a dg Hom formula by itself computes derived Hom.

source.place: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.localization (line 89), localization_unit_app (118), localization_counit_app (125); categories.tex Tag 04VG for localization

proof.text: For $T=U\cap V$ and a dg module $P$ on $U$, construct a dg map $b_P:j'_!(P|_T)\to(JP)|_V$ using the ordinary dg adjunction for $j'$ from [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-open-extension-adjunction]. Its transpose is the canonical identity $P|_T\to(JP)|_T$ induced by $\eta_P$. It is natural in $P$. By [lem-sc-module-extension-by-zero-stalk-maps](1), at $x\in T$ both complexes have stalk $P_x$ and $b_P$ is the identity; at $x\in V\setminus T$ both are zero. Thus in every degree $b_P$ is a stalkwise bijection, hence a sheaf isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks]. Its degreewise inverse is module-linear, commutes with differentials and actions by multiplying the corresponding commutative equations by the inverse maps. Thus $b$ is a dg natural isomorphism. Its inverse, followed by localization, is exactly the asserted $k^*j_!\simeq j'_!k'^*$.

For $W\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$, the ordinary dg adjunction for $ji$ gives a canonical map $c_P:(ji)_!P\to j_!i_!P$ whose transpose is the identity identification $P\to(j_!i_!P)|_W$ from the two units. The stalk formula of [lem-sc-module-extension-by-zero-stalk-maps](1) makes $c_P$ the identity at every point of $W$ and the unique map between zero modules elsewhere, degree by degree. The stalk criterion [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks] makes it a degreewise sheaf isomorphism; as in step 9 its inverse is a dg map. This natural dg isomorphism induces the required composition isomorphism in $D$.

The maps of steps 9 and 10 are normalized to the identity on the open where the original module is defined, as are the unit and the restricted counit of step 1. In a diagram comparing these identifications with a unit or counit, or comparing iterated restriction and composition identifications, its source stalk is either that original module stalk, where both paths are the identity, or zero, where the two paths are the unique map from zero. Hence the degreewise sheaf maps along the two paths agree: for a section, equality of all image germs gives an open cover on which its images coincide, and the sheaf separation axiom gives equality of sections. This proves the underived coherence including identities, triple compositions and further open restrictions. These are equalities of dg maps, so remain equalities on $K$ and after localization. Naturality against a formal inverse follows from naturality against $w$ by composing with the inverses of its two images. Equivalently, the uniqueness assertion for localized natural transformations in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] propagates the same equalities to all localized morphisms. All constructions used only degreewise sheaf maps and finite sums, so impose none of the excluded finiteness, boundedness or flatness conditions.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary sheaf-module exactness on an arbitrary ringed space is a generic tool; the dg node of this unit states the adjunction but not exactness.
Ordinary module extension stalks identify the zero and identity stalks used in the dg base-change and composition maps; no dg adjunction alone states these stalk formulas.
Generic triangulated localization supplies additive localization and the isomorphic-image description, after the same-unit dg homotopy-system theorem verifies its hypotheses.
Generic additive-localization descent proves additivity of the two factored dg functors, after the actual additive localization has been constructed.
The generic localization universal property descends the actual dg functors and transformations; it replaces no geometric step of the unit.
The sheaf-of-sets stalk criterion on an arbitrary space proves the constructed degreewise maps are invertible; scheme-only module versions would not apply.

lean.statement: theorem open_extension_calculus (A : Algebra S) (U : Opens X) : (openExtension.{u, w} A U).Additive ∧ (restriction A U).Additive ∧ (∀ (P P' : LeftModule (restrictAlgebra A U)) (f g : P ⟶ P'), homotopyRel (restrictAlgebra A U) f g → homotopyRel A ((openExtension.{u, w} A U).map f) ((openExtension.{u, w} A U).map g)) ∧ (∀ (M M' : LeftModule A) (f g : M ⟶ M'), homotopyRel A f g → homotopyRel (restrictAlgebra A U) ((restriction A U).map f) ((restriction A U).map g)) ∧ (∀ (P P' : LeftModule (restrictAlgebra A U)) (f : P ⟶ P'), QuasiIso f.hom → QuasiIso ((openExtension.{u, w} A U).map f).hom) ∧ (∀ (M M' : LeftModule A) (f : M ⟶ M'), QuasiIso f.hom → QuasiIso ((restriction A U).map f).hom) ∧ (∀ (P : LeftModule (restrictAlgebra A U)) (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ U → Subsingleton (↥(colimit ((OpenNhds.inclusion x).op ⋙ ((openExtend.{u, w} A U P).X.X n).val.presheaf) : AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}))) ∧ IsIso (openAdjunction.{u, w} A U).unit ∧ (∀ M : LeftModule A, (openAdjunction.{u, w} A U).unit.app ((restriction A U).obj M) ≫ (restriction A U).map ((openAdjunction.{u, w} A U).counit.app M) = 𝟙 _) ∧ IsIso (derivedOpenAdjunction.{u, w} A U).unit ∧ (∀ M : Derived A, (derivedOpenAdjunction.{u, w} A U).unit.app ((derivedRestriction A U).obj M) ≫ (derivedRestriction A U).map ((derivedOpenAdjunction.{u, w} A U).counit.app M) = 𝟙 _)
